title: Examine one interaction
opening: When you examine your own movement, the teammate is outside your body. In the team drill, that same teammate is inside the system.

labels.demoIntro: Suppose changing the drill space improves a player's return but makes the partner's participation unworkable. If the ball feed and task also change, the results cannot be pinned on space alone.
labels.comparisonIntro: Suppose changing the drill space improves a player's return but makes the partner's participation unworkable. If the ball feed and task also change, the results cannot be pinned on space alone.
labels.playerText: Within the boundary: the player's movement and response. Outside it: the partner and the shared drill arrangement. A partner's action is external to the player.
labels.teamText: Within the boundary: both players, their actions and the shared drill arrangement. The partner's action is inside the team system. Conditions beyond the drill remain outside this boundary.
labels.playerBoundary: Within the boundary: the player's movement and response. Outside it: the partner and the shared drill arrangement. A partner's action is external to the player.
labels.teamBoundary: Within the boundary: both players, their actions and the shared drill arrangement. The partner's action is inside the team system. Conditions beyond the drill remain outside this boundary.
labels.returnRoles: The player is the agent acting on the ball, the target, with the racket as the instrument. The partner participates in the drill. The available court space is a condition of the interaction. Those roles stay the same when you change the boundary.
labels.authorityGroup: Can you make a bounded change to the drill?
labels.authorityYes: I have authority to change one condition
labels.conditionsGroup: What else changes during the comparison?
labels.steady: Keep the ball feed and task steady
labels.confounded: The ball feed and task also change
labels.predictResponse: The available time to respond may change
labels.predictPartner: The partner's participation may change too
labels.notRecorded: No trial data is supplied. Keep a prediction separate from an observation.
labels.demoResultTitle: What the comparison can tell you
labels.observeOnlyResult: Without authority to change the drill, observe the feed, task and players within your chosen boundary. You can record what happened, but cannot test the effect of your proposed change.
labels.steadyResult: The source explains that changing space can change the time available to respond. That is a prediction, not a result. Keep the feed and task steady, make one bounded change, then compare an actual result with your prediction.
labels.confoundedResult: The feed and task changed along with the space. You can describe the whole drill as changed, but cannot isolate space as the cause. Record each change before revising the explanation.
labels.predictionNote: A prediction describes what you expect. It is not an observation or a result.
labels.practice: Map one interaction of your own
labels.practiceIntro: State the boundary and result. Separate observation from assumption, then name one accessible condition, its predicted effect and any side effect.
labels.private: This private note is optional. The six required course questions are separate.
labels.sampleLoaded: Authored example loaded. Replace it with your own observations when useful.
labels.length: This full note is over 2,000 characters. Shorten it to save; all of your text stays here.
labels.sourceQuote: When you examine your own movement, your body is the system. When you examine your team, you and the other players are parts of that system. Another player’s action is outside you but inside your team. Choose the system before you call a cause internal or external.

feedback.unavailable: Private saving is unavailable. Your note stays on screen.
feedback.length: Shorten the full note to fit the 2,000-character limit. Your text stays here.
feedback.conflict: This note changed elsewhere. Your answers remain here; compare the saved version before saving again.
feedback.readFailure: The saved note could not be loaded.
feedback.readbackFailure: The save could not be confirmed. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.saveFailure: The save is uncertain. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.retryPending: The earlier save is unresolved. Retry the same note before changing it.

fields.label: What system boundary and result are you examining?
What constraints, environment, entities and mechanism matter?
Who acts, what receives the action, and which instruments or bystanders matter?
What one accessible condition would you change, and what effect and side effect do you predict?
What actually happened, and what else changed at the same time?

example.boundary: Examine a tennis practice interaction: a player's return and the partner's ability to take part in the drill.
example.conditions: The source example names available space, ball feed and task. These conditions can affect the response and the partner's participation.
example.roles: The returning player acts on the incoming ball with a racket. The partner is affected by the shared drill arrangement.
example.prediction: Changing the available space may change the time to respond and may also change partner participation. This is a prediction, not a measured effect.
example.return: No trial is recorded. Keep feed and task steady if the question is about space; otherwise note all changes and do not assign the result to space alone.

source.assessmentBoundary: Six required open-ended questions remain separate from this optional private note. No qualified semantic grade or actual learner outcome is supplied.
